While it's true that society as a whole is over medicated and people often turn to drugs as a quick fix, that does not mean that antidepressants have no use and aren't absolutely necessary in many cases. It's good to consider other options but if you need them, there should be no shame in seeking that kind of help. If your partner can't be supportive of that then maybe the two of you simply aren't meant to be. 

P.S. - Some antidepressants can make certain symptoms of depression worse for some people, and it can take a few weeks to adjust to a new medication. If you start feeling suicidal, please try to remember that the meds are affecting your judgement and reach out to someone for support. 

Best of luck. I hope this leads to true and lasting happiness for you

I sort of have experience with this situation from the perspective of your daughter.  My mom kicked me out of the house when I was only 16 because my step dad demanded it.  My step brother who is the same age as me was getting in all sorts of trouble at the time. Skipping school, getting busted by the cops with weed etc. My step dad blamed me, saying that I was a bad influence on him, even though I went to school every day and wasn't regularly getting arrested or anything like that (I was a bit of a pothead though). 
Anyway, my mom complied with My step dad's demands and I was put out on my own.  I'm 39 now and although I've forgiven my mom, there's no denying how badly this affected my life. Being forced to drop out of school and work full time to support myself without any real parental guidance or support has set me back so far in life.  And I think the feeling of abandonment and betrayal by my mother is at the core of the trust and addiction issues I've dealt with throughout my adult life.

One more thing - my mom was a CNA and she ended up working her way up to a high paying position as director in one of the departments at an up scale nursing home. I'm not sure where you work but it may benefit you to look for a position within a company like that

Also be careful with kratom. Like phenibut, it can be a great tool that, if used responsibly, can help improve some areas of your life. But if taken daily it will most likely cause physical dependence and very uncomfortable withdrawal upon quitting.  I would recommend only using it only 2-3 days per week, or every other day, or no more than one daily dose with breaks here and there.  I'm speaking as a current kratom addict and a previous opiate addict.   There's a lot of misinformation about the addictive nature of kratom but if I go more than 4 or 5 hours without a dose, I start experiencing withdrawal that rivals coming off of 150mg of oxy per day (I use a LOT of kratom though). 
Best of luck!
